'''Roy James Cameron''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|CB}} (11 March 1923{{spaced endash}}3 October 2006) was an Australian public servant and [[diplomat]]. He was the [[Australian Statistician]] from 1977 to 1985.

==Life and career==
Cameron was born in [[Port Pirie]], [[South Australia]] on 11 March 1923. He studied at the [[University of Adelaide]], graduating with first class honours from a Bachelor of Economics course in 1948. He graduated a Master of Economics from the university in 1951, with the topic "Standard hours and the basic wage: an analysis of two aspects of the work of the Commonwealth Court of Conciliation and Arbitration."<ref name=Trewin>{{citation|url=http://www.statsoc.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/SSAI-118-web-small.pdf|title=Obituaries: Roy James Cameron 11th March 1923 – 3 October 2006|first=Dennis|last=Trewin|author-link=Dennis Trewin|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150316123227/http://www.statsoc.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/SSAI-118-web-small.pdf|archivedate=16 March 2015 |date=March 2007|journal=Statistical Society of Australia Incorporated|issue=118}}</ref> He was awarded a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright]] scholarship to study for his doctorate at [[Harvard University]], starting in 1951.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.fulbright.com.au/index.php/partners/featured-partners|title=Featured Partners|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160326065029/http://www.fulbright.com.au/index.php/partners/featured-partners|archivedate=26 March 2016|publisher=Australian American Fulbright Commission}}</ref> He completed his PhD in 1956.<ref name=Trewin/>

From 1973 to 1977 Cameron was Australia's Ambassador to the [[Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development]] in Paris. His appointment announcement, which was issued by [[Gough Whitlam]] in 1973, noted Cameron's broad experience in economic and financial matters.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://pmtranscripts.dpmc.gov.au/sites/default/files/original/00002894.pdf|title=Ambassador to the O.E.C.D.|date=12 April 1973|publisher=Australian Government|first=Edward Gough|last=Whitlam|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816124203/https://pmtranscripts.dpmc.gov.au/sites/default/files/original/00002894.pdf|archivedate=16 August 2016|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

In 1977 Cameron returned to Australia to take up his appointment as [[Australian Statistician]]. He served in the role until his retirement in August&nbsp;1985.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article131803120 |title=New statistician named |newspaper=The Canberra Times|date=24 December 1976 |page=1}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/news/obituaries/he-shaped-how-we-view-society/2006/10/19/1160851062049.html?page=fullpage#contentSwap1|newspaper=The Sydney Morning Herald|date=20 October 2006|title=He shaped how we view society|archivedate=14 July 2016|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160714085749/http://www.smh.com.au/news/obituaries/he-shaped-how-we-view-society/2006/10/19/1160851062049.html?page=fullpage|first=Dennis|last=Trewin|author-link=Dennis Trewin}}</ref>

Cameron died on 3 October 2006.<ref name=Trewin/>

==Awards==
Cameron was made a [[Companion of the Order of the Bath]] in the [[1982 Birthday Honours]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1064276|title=Search Australian Honours: CAMERON, Roy James, Award: The Order of the Bath - Companion (Civil)|publisher=Australian Government|work=itsanhonour.gov.au|archivedate=14 July 2016|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160714091256/http://www.itsanhonour.gov.au/honours/honour_roll/search.cfm?aus_award_id=1064276&search_type=quick&showInd=true}}</ref>
